picks.blurb: The Kennesaw State Owls (1-4, 0-1 CUSA) won this league last year and were expected to contend for the title again, but they've had a disappointing start to the year and have dropped back-to-back one-score games. Most recently, they lost 27-26 to Jacksonville State in their league opener. The Missouri State Bears (1-4, 0-1 CUSA), meanwhile, were a surprising bowl team last year in their first season at the FBS level. However, with a new coaching staff this season, they've struggled and are still looking for their first FBS win. Last week, they lost to a Western Kentucky game that looked like it could be the worst in the conference. If you are looking for some betting advice for the matchup, we've got you covered. Here are the latest odds for the game, courtesy of FanDuel. Still, he's the driving force behind this offense considering he also leads the way in a quarterback-centric rushing attack. That offense is a strength relative to the defense, which has been pretty rough overall, particularly against the pass. Missouri State's offense has its own issues, though, and it benched quarterback Skyler Locklear for Henry Belin IV last week. Still, this is an offense that doesn't run or pass particularly well, and its defense is arguably an even bigger weakness. It's hard to have much faith in Missouri State here, given how uncompetitive it was against Western Kentucky. The Bears are regrouping after a decisive 34-13 road loss to Western Kentucky, while the Owls hope to rebound from a heartbreaking 27-26 defeat at the hands of Jacksonville State. My Kennesaw State vs Missouri State prediction weighs the rushing matchup against two offenses looking for a more complete performance. The win prices and a separate total pick follow. The Owls average 376.4 total yards per game with a rushing attack churning out 157.0 yards at a healthy 4.73 per carry. Missouri State is the wrong opponent for that. The Bears surrender 449.6 total yards and 32.4 points per game, and they get gashed on the ground specifically, allowing 196.4 rushing yards at 4.77 per carry. Rickie Collins is the engine for Kennesaw State. He has passed for 1,042 yards while adding 246 rushing yards and four touchdowns, giving the Owls a quarterback who can extend drives with his legs when the pocket breaks down. He has help behind him too. Boogie Woods III and Latrelle Murrell combine to average 5.2 yards a carry, which is exactly the profile you want against a front allowing almost 200 rushing yards per game. Kennesaw State has scored just 22.6 points per game, but its last two losses came by one and three points. Against this defense, I like the Owls to turn another competitive game into a win. Plaster Stadium TV: CBS Sports Network | Watch Live RADIO: KSU Owl Network | Listen: KSU Owls App, Tune In | Online: KSUOwls.com | Satellite: SiriusXM 261 Team Info: Game Notes/Depth Charts | Clippings | 2026 Football Media Guide • Kennesaw State football looks to get back on track and even its Conference USA record when it heads to Springfield, Missouri for the second time in program history to take on Missouri State on Wednesday, Oct. 14 at Robert W. Plaster Stadium. • The Owls are coming off back-to-back heartbreaking one-score losses, falling 17-14 to Arkansas State and 27-26 to Jax State. The Bears have lost three-straight entering Wednesday, including a 34-13 defeat to WKU last week. • In its CUSA opener last week, Kennesaw State looked as good as it has offensively all season, recording the eighth-most FBS offensive yards in program history (411) and seventh-most passing yards (293) in a single game. • After averaging just 87 rushing yards against Georgia State and Tennessee, the Owls have found another gear, averaging 157 yards per game over their last two weeks. • Through five games, Kennesaw State ranks fourth in CUSA in points allowed (23.4), but has allowed just 18.8 points per game against non-Power 4 opponents. • Kennesaw State is the only CUSA team with four players who have rushed for at least 100 yards and a score in 2026 and one of only 20 teams in FBS. • Kennesaw State has scored at least 24 points in nine-straight regular-season conference games. • Sr. WR Brayden Munroe recorded the second-most receiving yards in program history last week against Jax State, hauling in seven catches for 159 yards -- second-most of any receiver in CUSA this season. • Munroe leads the team with 299 receiving yards on 19 catches, ranking sixth in the league with 59.8 receiving yards per game. • r-So. LB Tywon Christopher had a career night as well last week, recording 15 tackles, 2.0 tackles for loss and a forced fumble. He is one of only two players in FBS this season to record those numbers in a single game. • Kennesaw State has created havoc for teams this season, ranking second in the conference with seven turnovers gained (five fumble recoveries and two interceptions), and ranking 10th nationally (first in CUSA) with the five fumble recoveries. LogoParamountPlus More live games and exclusives Log Out Connect TV Provider More live games & exclusives Log Out Connect College Football News Transfer Portal 2027 Top Recruits 2027 Top Classes College Football Rankings Brad Crawford and Chris Hummer are back with their weekly picks and predictions for the weekend's best games Getty Images The Week 7 schedule features six top-25 matchups, giving contenders ample opportunity to strengthen their playoff cases before next month's first selection committee rankings . Nearing the midway point, preseason expectations now carry little weight -- ask teams like LSU, Texas &M, Michigan and Penn State -- with narratives already materializing. We're picking several of Saturday's showdowns that come with playoff implications, raising the stakes for teams in the SEC, Big Ten and Big 12 trying to protect unbeaten records . Ohio State-Indiana, Notre Dame-BYU, Alabama-Tennessee -- good luck finding a quiet window on this slate. Season results : Brad Crawford (38-13 straight up, 29-21-1 ATS); Chris Hummer (40-11 straight up, 27–23-1 ATS) We're coming off my personal worst picks week of my career straight up (3-5, yuck!) after a bevy of upsets I didn't see coming. The against-the-spread total wasn't fatal, at least. Hummer has narrowed the gap to two games back ATS and has assumed the lead straight up after a terrific showing. If these picks aren't enough this week, head to our CBS Sports expert picks page where Hummer's on a heater. No. 16 Mississippi State at No. 22 LSU (-10.5) Hummer ( LSU -10.5) : This game sets up for a LSU bounce back. Even if Kamario Taylor were healthy -- and his status is in doubt this week -- the Tigers have a lot of advantages in this game, including an elite secondary and pass rush. The big question for LSU is whether Sam Leavitt can avoid turnovers. If he plays clean, which has been a problem all year given that he leads the nation in INTs, LSU should roll. … LSU 38, Mississippi State 24. Crawford (LSU -10.5) : Is this the week LSU finally puts it together against an opponent of substance? It is time the Tigers look the part as a potential CFP team after two SEC losses already. A third ends any hope of getting to the 12-team bracket, even if LSU wins out from there and finishes 9-3. The resume simply won't be good enough to warrant enough attention. I'm giving this the must-win label for Lane Kiffin, whose first season is teetering on total disappointment if he's handed a third loss before playing Alabama in November. ... LSU 37, Mississippi State 20. Florida at No. 7 Texas (-9.5) Hummer ( Florida +9.5) : Which version of Arch Manning and the Texas passing attack are we going to get? That's going to determine whether Texas rolls in this game. The Gators have the worst pass defense in the SEC and have been torched by far less talented (on paper) passing attacks than Texas. But Texas has been incredibly inconsistent on offense this year, ranking just 62nd nationally in passing yards per game. Texas, a top-15 rushing defense, is set up to contain Jadan Baugh and Florida's rushing attack. But can it score enough to cover in this one? I'm extremely skeptical. Perhaps Texas responds and blows Florida out -- a real possibility -- but that's just not the team we've seen this year. … Texas 31, Florida 24. Crawford (Texas -9.5) : I'm not positive on this, but the public play will assuredly be Florida, given the potential hangover effect from the Longhorns' loss to Oklahoma . The Gators stink worse, though, with consecutive blowout losses in SEC play since starting the season 4-0 and ranked No. 8. Florida's secondary looks atrocious after being carved up by LaNorris Sellers last week and Arch Manning could do the same. Manning has been off more than sharp this fall, but this is a matchup I like for the Texas offense. The Longhorns lost to Florida last season, and that could play a role in Saturday's performance, too. ... Texas 34, Florida 24. No. 6 Alabama (-6.5) at No. 14 Tennessee Hummer (Alabama -6.5) : The Vols have survived this year behind an elite defense. That unit has carried an offense that ranks just 66th nationally in yards per play and 110th in passing yards per game. But is that defense good enough to hold off Alabama? I'm highly skeptical. Alabama's defense has been susceptible in the secondary this year. But the Vols don't have the passing offense to take advantage of that. The Crimson Tide roll in this game for a second straight year. … Alabama 24, Tennessee 17. Crawford (Alabama -6.5) : It almost feels disrespectful to call this a "get-right" game for the Crimson Tide given their recent struggles at Neyland Stadium, but unless DeSean Bishop controls this game on the ground for the Vols, I don't see a path to a Tennessee victory. The passing game is a struggle for Josh Heupel, and Alabama can score points in a hurry. Falling behind in the first half could lead to a chorus of boos in Knoxville if the Crimson Tide's defense can put together stops. This is a dangerous game for Tennessee, not so much the betting favorites even without Ryan Coleman-Williams on the outside. ... Alabama 30, Tennessee 17. No. 13 Missouri at No. 9 Ole Miss (-6.5) Hummer ( Missouri +6.5) : Ole Miss should have a detailed scouting report on Austin Simmons in this one given that Pete Golding faced him every day for years at Ole Miss. This game will tell us a lot about whether the Rebels' secondary is really any better after their blowout loss to Florida. Missouri is an excellent team. The Tigers are stout up front defensively and have a passing attack that can expose Ole Miss' defense. This game has a ton of star power crossover -- Kewan Lacy went from Missouri to Ole Miss, Simmons from Oxford to Columbia -- and I think it is close throughout. … Ole Miss 31, Missouri 28. Crawford (Missouri +6.5) : Is there anyone out there who saw this being a top-15 matchup a month ago? The Tigers' run without Ahmad Hardy has really been impressive. Jamal Roberts has back-to-back 200-yard outings on the ground and could easily have a third against a defense that's had its issues this season. I like Missouri in this spot with the points. I'm still not sure what to make of the Rebels outside of Trinidad Chambliss . You know what you're getting out of him, but Kewan Lacy is banged up and play on the other side of the football has left much to be desired. ... Ole Miss 30, Missouri 24. No. 18 Oklahoma State at No. 20 Houston (-3.5) Hummer ( Oklahoma State +3.5) : The Cowboys have gotten better every week this season to the point where, with their offense, you can really start to imagine them as an immediate Big 12 title threat. But this is by far their in Big 12 play. Houston is among the nation's best rushing attacks, and Oklahoma State is among the least successful run defenses in the country on a down-to-down basis. Houston plays more zone coverage than any other Big 12 team to prevent big plays. Houston's secondary hasn't succeeded in that area, given the Cougars' rank of 126th nationally in passes allowed of 20-plus yards. This game will come down to two areas: 1. Can Houston control the clock and convert in the red zone? 2. Can Oklahoma State create chunk plays in the passing game? I'm not willing to pick the outright upset here, but I think the Cowboys are in position to have a lot of offensive success in this one. … Houston 31, Oklahoma State 28. Crawford (Oklahoma State +3.5) : Oklahoma State's path to an upset starts with explosive plays while trying to keep Conner Weigman contained on the other side of the football. The Cowboys don't need to dominate every snap if they're turning opportunities into chunk plays and touchdowns. Force Houston to chase points, and suddenly the pressure shifts to the favorite at home in front of what Willie Fritz hopes will be a sellout crowd. This is a matchup with significant Big 12 title game implications, especially since the Cougars already have a loss in conference play at Texas Tech . ... Oklahoma State 34, Houston 31. Penn State at Michigan (-5.5) Hummer (Michigan -5.5) : The losing coach in this one is going to be feeling very uncomfortable. If Penn State falls, it'll be four straight dropped games. If Michigan loses, the Wolverines will have lost three in a row and will be out of the playoff hunt before the calendar turns to November. Michigan will have to run to win in this one. The Nittany Lions have an excellent secondary and, to be kind, Michigan's passing attack has been far from a strength. The good news for the Wolverines is that the Nittany Lions rank 113th nationally in yards allowed per carry. Coming out of a bye -- and given Penn State's struggles to run the football -- I like the Wolverines to cover. … Michigan 27, Penn State 21. Crawford (Penn State +5.5) : Neither of these teams has won a game in the Big Ten, and it's mid-October. That's unacceptable for two first-year staffs at these respective blueblood programs. picks.blurb: Ohio State @ Indiana Preview And Prediction - Yahoo Sports Search Query for Search Search Home News Finance Sports More Mail NCAAF College Fantasy Football College Football Playoff Brewers take 3-0 NLCS lead NFL hot seats Champions League results Heisman Watch Ohio State @ Indiana Preview And Prediction Indiana Hoosiers linebacker Isaiah Jones (46) works to bring down Ohio State Buckeyes quarterback Julian Sayin (10) on Saturday, Dec. 6, 2025, during the Big Ten football championship at Lucas Oil Stadium in Indianapolis. Landon Kardian Tue, October 13, 2026 at 6:44 PM UTC · 3 min read Advertisement Advertisement About Our Ads College Sports Sports Business Women's Sports College & High School Adventure Sports What & How To Watch Responsible Gaming Share Your Feedback About Our Ads No. 4 Ohio State travels to No. 5 Indiana for a massive Big Noon showdown. Can the Buckeyes avenge last year's Big Ten Championship loss? One of the biggest games of the college football season is set for Saturday afternoon as No. 4 Ohio State travels to Bloomington to take on No. 5 Indiana in FOX's Big Noon Saturday showdown. And there is plenty of bad blood between these two programs. The last time these teams met, Indiana stunned Ohio State 13-10 in the 2025 Big Ten Championship Game, ending the Buckeyes' undefeated season. Now, Ryan Day and Ohio State have an opportunity to return the favor against Curt Cignetti's defending national champions. Ohio State enters at 5-1, while Indiana remains undefeated at 6-0. Both teams are 3-0 in Big Ten play, making this matchup potentially decisive in the conference championship race. Ohio State: Can Julian Sayin Deliver? Ohio State's offense has been explosive this season, averaging more than 42 points per game. Quarterback Julian Sayin has thrown for approximately 1,772 yards, while superstar wide receiver Jeremiah Smith has been nearly unstoppable, recording 48 receptions for 916 yards and 11 touchdowns. Smith is the most dangerous player in college football, and Indiana's secondary will have its hands full trying to contain him. However, last year's championship game exposed some serious problems for Ohio State. Sayin threw for 258 yards, and Smith recorded eight catches for 144 yards, but the Buckeyes managed just 10 points. Sayin was also sacked five times. Indiana's defensive front remains dangerous, averaging 3.3 sacks and 8.2 tackles for loss per game this season. Running back Bo Jackson, who has rushed for approximately 460 yards, must help establish balance and prevent Indiana from focusing entirely on Sayin. Indiana: The Hoosiers Aren't Going Anywhere Indiana might have lost Heisman Trophy winner Fernando Mendoza, but Curt Cignetti has kept the Hoosiers rolling. TCU transfer Josh Hoover has thrown for more than 1,300 yards with 17 touchdowns and zero interceptions, while running back Turbo Richard has rushed for nearly 600 yards. Wide receiver Charlie Becker has also been outstanding, recording 529 receiving yards and eight touchdowns. Michigan State transfer Nick Marsh gives Indiana another dangerous weapon on the outside. Defensively, Indiana is allowing approximately 12 points per game and has demonstrated an ability to create pressure without sacrificing coverage. However, the Hoosiers haven't exactly dominated their recent competition. Indiana narrowly escaped Northwestern 29-23 before defeating Nebraska 20-17 last weekend. Those performances raise questions about whether the Hoosiers can consistently move the football against an elite opponent. Expect another physical, defensive battle between two legitimate College Football Playoff contenders. Indiana's defense will create problems for Sayin, and the Hoosiers should find success moving the football through Hoover and Richard. However, Ohio State has something Indiana doesn't: Jeremiah Smith. I expect Smith to deliver a massive performance, surpassing 100 receiving yards and making the difference in a game that comes down to the final possession. Sayin will make a few mistakes under pressure, but the Buckeyes' defense will get enough stops to escape Bloomington with a huge victory. Final Score: No. 4 Ohio State 24, No. 5 Indiana 20 Ohio State gets its revenge, hands Indiana its first loss of the season, and puts itself in an excellent position in the Big Ten championship race. picks.headline: Ohio State vs Indiana Prediction: Biggest Home Game In Hoosier History
picks.blurb: Ohio State vs Indiana Prediction: Biggest Home Game In Hoosier History - Yahoo Sports Search Query for Search Search Home News Finance Sports More Mail NCAAF College Fantasy Football College Football Playoff Brewers take 3-0 NLCS lead NFL hot seats Champions League results Heisman Watch Ohio State vs Indiana Prediction: Biggest Home Game In Hoosier History Advertisement Advertisement About Our Ads College Sports Sports Business Women's Sports College & High School Adventure Sports What & How To Watch Responsible Gaming Share Your Feedback About Our Ads We're all over the whole It's Still Strange That Indiana Is Good At College Football thing, right? Not yet. The Hoosiers are 6-0. While that's hardly surprising with this team, it's just the 28th time in 128 years of IU football that it has won six games or more. Ohio State has played football for 115 years, and when it wins another game, it'll make it 90 seasons with six or more wins. Also, for all the games played in Bloomington against teams ranked in the top five, this is the first time in Indiana history that two top-five teams have faced each other in Memorial Stadium. There will be plenty of showdowns and big things happening over the second half of the season, but this is it. This is the Big Ten Game of the Year, and now we get to see if Indiana can keep the party going, or if Ohio State reestablish itself as the conference's top dog. Ohio State vs Indiana: Quick Hits Ohio State gets a week off before going to USC, and then four of the last five games are at home. This starts a run of three home games in four dates for Indiana, with a trip to Michigan next before hosting Minnesota and USC. Indiana won the last meeting over the Buckeyes in the 2025 Big Ten Championship. Ohio State had won the previous 30 games and is 61-3-2 in the series since 1951. How To Watch Ohio State vs Indiana Date: Saturday, October 17, 2026 Game Time: 12:00 PM ET TV: FOX Location: Memorial Stadium, Bloomington, IN – CFN Week 7 Schedule, Predictions – CFN Top 25 | Bowl Projections – Predictions For Every Remaining Game – CFN Week 7 Expert Picks Why Ohio State Will Win This isn't the Indiana team of last year, especially offensively. The Hoosiers are smart, don't make mistakes, and the coaching is still peerless, but Josh Hoover – as good as he is – isn't Fernando Mendoza. He's not as accurate, the running game isn't as strong, and because of it, the team isn't moving the ball quite as well. It's still a fantastic attack with plenty of explosion, but this year's team is 40th in the nation on third downs, connecting at a 45% clip. Last year's team was automatic – it was No. 1 in the country, hitting a whopping 56.5% of its third-down tries. The other key difference? Takeaways. Last year's Hoosier defense forced ten turnovers over the first six games. This year's version has come up with just four, with just one in the three Big Ten games. Oct 10, 2026; Columbus, Ohio, USA; Ohio State Buckeyes wide receiver Jeremiah Smith (4) celebrates his touchdown with Ohio State Buckeyes wide receiver Brock Boyd (11) during the first quarter against the Maryland Terrapins at Ohio Stadium. Mandatory Credit: Joseph Maiorana-Imagn Images Why Indiana Will Win This isn't the Ohio State team of last year, especially defensively. And throw in the running game, too. Who wants to run the ball when you have Jeremiah Smith to throw to? But this has now become a problem in big games. Last year, Ohio State failed to run for 90 yards three times – the losses to Indiana and Miami, and the close-call 14-7 win over Texas. Indiana's run defense is allowing just 2.3 yards per carry. But it's the other side that's the real issue – relatively speaking for Ohio State. This defense is fantastic. It's just not the next-level killer of past seasons. The Buckeyes are struggling to come up with third-down stops. There's little to no pass rush, and despite being fourth in the nation in total defense, so far it has allowed more than 16 points three times. How many times did it allow that many points last year? Once – Miami 24, Ohio State 14. How about in 2024? Three times. Twice to an Oregon team that went 13-1, and in the national championship against Notre Dame. Ohio State vs Indiana Prediction, Betting Lines Enough about what these teams aren't. They're both national championship-level good, but there's a Prove It factor here. Indiana was able to keep its cool and come through late in the win over Nebraska, and not flinch when Northwestern was making a charge in the second half. Ohio State had one fourth quarter against Texas when it buckled, but when it was on against Iowa, the big, bad Buckeyes flexed hard with a nearly perfect performance. Curt Cignetti will work magic with a game plan that will keep this close. It'll seem like Ohio State is dominating, but a missed field goal here, an empty trip there, and it'll be hard to put the game away. And then Josh Hoover will pick the wrong time to throw his first interception of the season. away.headline: Ohio State football releases first injury report vs. Indiana: Who’s in, who’s out for the Buckeyes
away.blurb: Offensive lineman Austin Siereveld, who missed last week’s win against Maryland, was deemed out on Wednesday’s injury report — the first of four reports this week. Running back Ja’Kobi Jackson, who has appeared in every game for the Buckeyes this season, was also listed as out. He has started the last two games for Ohio State, though running back Bo Jackson had more carries in both contests. Receiver Brock Boyd, running back Isaiah West, defensive end Khary Wilder and offensive lineman Deontae Armstrong were listed as questionable. Linebacker Christian Alliegro, defensive back Jay Timmons, offensive tackle Phillip Daniels and receivers Devin McCuin and Brandon Inniss were not on the report, suggesting they’ll be available after missing last week’s win vs. Maryland. While Timmons could return this week, safety Leroy Roker — who has also been sidelined since Sept. 26 — was listed as out. COLUMBUS, Ohio — Ohio State plays at Indiana on Saturday in one of the biggest games of the college football regular season. Pete Fiutak Wed, October 14, 2026 at 6:42 PM UTC · 4 min read Advertisement Advertisement About Our Ads College Sports Sports Business Women's Sports College & High School Adventure Sports What & How To Watch Responsible Gaming Share Your Feedback About Our Ads Just a few weeks ago, Florida was coming off a 52-28 obliteration of a terrific Ole Miss team, and everything was wonderful. The Gators appeared good enough in the first season under Jon Sumrall to be in the SEC and College Football Playoff mix, the offense was unstoppable, and then a funny thing happened. The SEC figured it out. Missouri and South Carolina beat Florida by a combined score of 83-36, and now, with the schedule ahead, the 4-2 team might have to fight just to get to a bowl game. Last week at this time, Texas was No. 1, it was about to play a punchless Oklahoma team, and then a funny thing happened. The Sooners came up with creative and clutch ways to pull off a 27-24 Red River Rivalry win. The season is hardly over for the Longhorns, but now there's little margin for error over a tough second half. Florida vs Texas: Quick Hits It doesn't get any easier for Florida after this, with a week off before dealing with Georgia, followed up by Oklahoma, and then a trip to Kentucky. Can Arch Manning silence his critics and save the Longhorns' season? No. 7 Texas (4-1) returns home Saturday afternoon to face Florida (4-2) in a massive SEC matchup between two programs desperate for a bounce-back victory. The Longhorns are coming off an embarrassing 27-24 loss to Oklahoma, while Florida was dominated 38-19 at home by South Carolina. Both teams entered the season with championship aspirations, but another loss could seriously damage their College Football Playoff hopes. And for Texas quarterback Arch Manning, the pressure has never been higher. Texas: It's Time for Arch Manning to Deliver Manning entered the season as one of the Heisman Trophy favorites, but his performances have been anything but consistent. Through five games, Manning has thrown for 1,122 yards, 10 touchdowns, and five interceptions. Against Oklahoma, he completed 19 of 31 passes for 260 yards and three touchdowns, but two costly fourth-quarter interceptions helped the Sooners erase a 17-7 halftime deficit. The Longhorns are averaging just 379.2 yards per game, ranking 79th nationally. That's simply unacceptable considering the offensive talent Steve Sarkisian has assembled. However, Saturday presents an excellent opportunity to get things back on track. Florida's defense is allowing 393 yards and 29 points per game, including an alarming 268.7 passing yards per contest. Wide receiver Cam Coleman, who has 318 receiving yards and five touchdowns, should have opportunities to create explosive plays against a struggling Gators secondary. Defensively, Texas has been outstanding, allowing just 16 points and 96 rushing yards per game. Edge rusher Colin Simmons has been nearly unstoppable, recording 9.5 sacks. Florida: Can Jadan Baugh Save the Gators? Florida's offense has actually been impressive this season, averaging 41.7 points and 473.8 yards per game. Quarterback Aaron Philo has thrown for 1,341 yards, nine touchdowns, and three interceptions, while receiver Dallas Wilson has recorded 376 yards and three touchdowns. However, the biggest storyline is running back Jadan Baugh. Baugh has rushed for 672 yards and 12 touchdowns, establishing himself as one of the SEC's most productive backs. Unfortunately, his production has slowed considerably. Over Florida's last two games, Baugh has managed just 72 rushing yards, including 59 yards on 15 carries against South Carolina. That's a major concern considering Texas possesses one of the nation's best rushing defenses. Florida also defeated Texas 29-21 last season, meaning the Gators have already proven they're capable of beating Sarkisian's program. But winning in Austin will be a completely different challenge. How Each Team Wins For Texas, the formula starts with protecting Manning and establishing an early rhythm through the passing game. The Longhorns must take advantage of Florida's vulnerable secondary while allowing their defensive front to disrupt Philo and contain Baugh. For Florida, everything revolves around getting Baugh going early. If the Gators can establish their rushing attack, they'll have opportunities to control possession and keep Manning on the sidelines. Defensively, Florida must force Manning into mistakes, something Oklahoma successfully accomplished last weekend. I expect Texas to respond with a much more disciplined performance following its disappointing loss to Oklahoma. Manning should have opportunities to attack Florida's secondary, but I'm still not convinced he's capable of consistently dominating SEC competition. Expect a solid, rather than spectacular, performance from the Texas quarterback. The biggest difference will be Texas' defense. With Simmons creating pressure and the Longhorns limiting Baugh's rushing opportunities, Florida will struggle to sustain drives throughout the afternoon. I expect the Gators to keep things competitive early, but Texas will gradually take control in the second half. Final Score: No. 7 Texas 27, Florida 17 Texas gets back in the win column, improves to 5-1, and keeps its College Football Playoff hopes alive. Lane Kiffin's Tigers are coming off an embarrassing 35-34 overtime loss to Kentucky, a game LSU had every opportunity to win before a questionable fourth-down decision allowed the Wildcats to force overtime. Meanwhile, Mississippi State is looking to bounce back after a disappointing loss to Alabama. With LSU already sitting at 1-2 in SEC play, another conference loss could effectively end the Tigers' College Football Playoff hopes. LSU: Can Sam Leavitt Save the Tigers? LSU's offense has shown flashes of brilliance under Kiffin, but consistency remains a major concern. Quarterback Sam Leavitt has thrown for 1,495 yards and 10 touchdowns, but his eight interceptions are the most of any quarterback in the SEC. Those turnovers have been a major issue for a team that possesses enough offensive talent to compete with nearly anyone. Running back Dilin Jones has provided stability in the backfield, rushing for 426 yards and five touchdowns through LSU's first five games. Wide receiver Winston Watkins Jr. has also emerged as a dangerous weapon, recording 354 receiving yards. Defensively, LSU has been impressive at times, particularly with edge rusher Princewill Umanmielen, who recorded eight sacks through the team's first five games. However, the Tigers just surrendered 35 points to Kentucky, raising serious questions about their ability to close out games. Against Mississippi State's explosive offense, LSU cannot afford another inconsistent defensive performance. Mississippi State: Kamario Taylor Is a PROBLEM Jeff Lebby has Mississippi State playing some exciting football, and quarterback Kamario Taylor has emerged as one of the SEC's most dangerous young players. Taylor has thrown for 1,450 yards, 17 touchdowns, and just four interceptions while completing 66.2% of his passes. However, his availability is a major concern after aggravating a lower-leg injury against Alabama. If Taylor is healthy enough to play, LSU's defense will have its hands full. Wide receiver Anthony Evans III has been outstanding, recording 40 receptions for 574 yards and five touchdowns through five games. Running back Fluff Bothwell has also been productive, rushing for 403 yards and three touchdowns while averaging 5.4 yards per carry. The Bulldogs possess enough offensive firepower to challenge LSU, but their defense remains vulnerable. Mississippi State was allowing 28 points and nearly 380 yards per game through its first five contests. That's a dangerous weakness against a Kiffin-led offense playing at home. Establishing Jones early should also create opportunities for explosive passing plays. Defensively, LSU needs to pressure Taylor if he plays and prevent Evans from creating big plays downfield. For Mississippi State, the formula revolves around attacking LSU's defense with tempo and forcing Leavitt into mistakes. If Taylor is available, his dual-threat ability could create serious problems. The Bulldogs must also establish Bothwell to prevent LSU from focusing entirely on the passing game. I expect an offensive shootout in Baton Rouge. Mississippi State has enough offensive talent to create problems for LSU, particularly if Taylor is healthy enough to play. However, I believe this is a bounce-back opportunity for Kiffin and the Tigers. Leavitt should have success attacking Mississippi State's secondary, and I expect him to throw for more than 300 yards and three touchdowns. The Bulldogs will keep things competitive throughout the afternoon, but LSU's home-field advantage and offensive firepower should ultimately make the difference. Expect Mississippi State to threaten late before LSU's defense comes up with a crucial stop to secure the victory. Few people would have expected that, but it is reality as the No. 16 Bulldogs (4-1, 2-1 SEC) and the No. 22 Tigers (4-2, 1-2) prepare to meet Saturday in Baton Rouge, La. There is still a lot of football to be played, and Mississippi State's latest game, a 56-23 home loss to Alabama two weeks ago, demonstrated that the program isn't yet where it hopes to go. "We've got a ton of work to do," Bulldogs coach Jeff Lebby said. "We've got a huge challenge on Saturday morning, but the perception of what is going on here and the energy around our program and where we're going, not just where we're at, is really good. And so we've got to build on that." A victory over LSU would be a significant building block for a team that has road wins against Minnesota and South Carolina and defeated then-No. 19 Missouri three weeks ago. Star quarterback Kamario Taylor sustained a lower leg injury in the victory over Missouri and aggravated it in the loss against Alabama, bringing into question his availability for the matchup with LSU. "Wednesday's going to do all the talking," Lebby said in reference to the first game-week injury report when he was asked about Taylor's status. Parker "Billy" Puckett replaced Taylor late in the game against Alabama, but he and AJ Swann are listed as co-No.

Mandatory Credit: David Leong-Imagn Images Landon Kardian Tue, October 13, 2026 at 8:33 PM UTC · 3 min read Advertisement Advertisement About Our Ads College Sports Sports Business Women's Sports College & High School Adventure Sports What & How To Watch Responsible Gaming Share Your Feedback About Our Ads No. 1 Georgia hosts Auburn in the Deep South's Oldest Rivalry. After dominating Alabama physically, the Bulldogs could embarrass the Tigers. The Deep South's Oldest Rivalry returns to Athens this Saturday as No. 1 Georgia (6-0) welcomes Auburn (3-2) to Sanford Stadium for a 3:30 p.m. ET showdown on ESPN. And this matchup could get ugly quickly. Kirby Smart's Bulldogs are coming off an impressive 20-17 road victory over Alabama, while Auburn suffered a disappointing 24-14 loss at Tennessee. Georgia has also won nine consecutive meetings against Auburn, including last year's 20-10 victory in Jordan-Hare Stadium. Georgia: The Bulldogs Are Built DIFFERENT Georgia might have delivered its most impressive performance of the season against Alabama. Despite missing its top two running backs, Nate Frazier and Chauncey Bowens, the Bulldogs rushed for 206 yards against one of the SEC's most talented defenses. Dwight Phillips Jr. stepped up in a major way, while Bo Walker provided additional production in the backfield. Quarterback Gunner Stockton was outstanding, completing 18 of 22 passes for 249 yards while accounting for two touchdowns. Through six games, Stockton has thrown for 1,298 yards and 14 touchdowns, completing more than 76% of his passes. Defensively, Georgia held Alabama quarterback Keelon Russell to just 185 passing yards while recording four sacks. With Chris Cole, Raylen Wilson, KJ Bolden, and Ellis Robinson IV leading the defense, Georgia has the personnel to completely overwhelm Auburn's offense. Auburn: Can the Tigers Even Keep This Competitive? Auburn enters Saturday with serious questions surrounding its offense. Quarterback Byrum Brown has thrown for approximately 1,055 yards with seven touchdowns and seven interceptions. While he's dangerous with his legs, his decision-making has been inconsistent. Against Tennessee, Brown rushed for 107 yards but threw two interceptions in the 24-14 loss. Wide receiver Keshaun Singleton has emerged as a reliable target, recording 29 receptions for 322 yards. However, Auburn's biggest concern might be its inability to consistently stop the run. Tennessee rushed for 237 yards against the Tigers last weekend. That's a terrible sign considering Georgia just rushed for more than 200 yards against Alabama without its top two backs. If Auburn can't contain Georgia's rushing attack, this game could be over by halftime. How Each Team Wins For Georgia, the formula is simple: establish the running game, control the line of scrimmage, and force Brown to beat its defense through the air. Stockton should have plenty of opportunities to attack Auburn's secondary once the Tigers begin loading the box. Defensively, Georgia must contain Brown's mobility and force him into obvious passing situations. For Auburn, everything starts with avoiding turnovers and creating explosive plays. Brown must use his legs to extend drives, while the Tigers' defense needs to generate pressure on Stockton. Auburn cannot afford to fall behind early and become one-dimensional. I don't see this game being particularly competitive. Georgia is coming off an emotional victory over Alabama, but Kirby Smart has built a program that rarely overlooks inferior opponents, especially rivals. The Bulldogs should dominate the line of scrimmage, and I expect another massive rushing performance regardless of whether Frazier and Bowens return. Stockton should have an efficient afternoon, throwing multiple touchdowns while Georgia's defense forces Brown into at least two turnovers. Expect the Bulldogs to establish a commanding lead before halftime and eventually begin rotating younger players into the game. Final Score: No. 1 Georgia 41, Auburn 10 Georgia dominates its oldest rival, improves to 7-0, and continues looking like the team to beat in college football. picks.blurb: Auburn's date with Georgia will be its second of four games against a ranked team on its October schedule. The Tigers failed their first test by losing to No. 14 Tennessee in Week 5, 24-14. Auburn will also face No. 21 LSU and No. 10 Ole Miss before the calendar flips to November. Georgia handled its first true test last Saturday, defeating No. 6 Alabama on the road, 20-17. The win, in addition to Texas' loss to unranked Oklahoma, pushed Georgia to the No. 1 spot in both the US LBM Coaches Poll and the Associated Press poll ahead of Week 7. picks.blurb: Georgia vs Auburn early odds give UGA a chance to prove Vegas wrong Skip to main content About Georgia Football Georgia Basketball FanSided NCAA Sites Georgia Football Recruiting Georgia All-Time Football Lists Georgia Basketball Recruiting Georgia All-Time Basketball Lists Georgia just beat Alabama on the road 20-17, but they don't have a lot of time to celebrate because they get Auburn at home next week in their first rivalry game of the season. Vegas is already weighing in on this game, and they unsurprisingly predict Georgia will win. In fact, Vegas believes Georgia will win by a wide margin, but they don't think it will be by as many points as Georgia has been winning throughout most of this season. Georgia football vs Auburn early odds Georgia is favored over Auburn by 18.5 points according to the DraftKings Sportsbook. The over-under for this matchup is set at 49.5 points as well. ESPN is high on Georgia's chance in this game as well as they give the Bulldogs a 90.3 percent chance to win this game. Outside of the Alabama game Georgia has won every game by at least 24 points. Auburn is much closer to the level of the five other teams that Georgia's blown out this season, but Vegas for some reason doesn't think UGA will win by as wide of a margin. This could be something Georgia could use to motivate themselves to try and show Vegas they can still blow teams out even after barely beating Alabama. Georgia will be playing Auburn with some added pressure There will be some added pressure on Georgia during this game. The Bulldogs just earned one of the best wins in all of college football by beating Alabama on the road, so now the expectations are for them to cruise the rest of the season especially against lesser competition. That will be the case even more so this week since Georgia will likely be the new No. 1 team in the country thanks to Texas' upset loss to Oklahoma. Georgia already had a target on their back this season after winning the SEC two years in a row, but that target grew even bigger after beating Alabama. Being the No. 1 team in the country though will make that target as large as possible. Auburn would love nothing more than to come into Athens and beat Georgia, so they undoubtedly will bring their best game. It is up to Georgia though to not get in their heads and focus on the task at hand because while beating Alabama is nice, they still haven't actually accomplished anything yet this season. Auburn could push Georgia more than they'd like to admit Auburn is 3-2 entering this game after coming off their bye week. That means the Tigers will be more fresh than Georgia which gives them a bit of an advantage, but Georgia is still expected to win easily. Auburn however has also kept things close with Georgia in recent years. Last year Georgia only beat Auburn 20-10. Auburn had a 10-0 lead and nearly made it 17-0 before halftime, but a fumble on the goal line propelled Georgia to score 20 unanswered points and win. The last time these teams played in Athens the Bulldogs won rather easily 31-13, but three years ago Georgia only won 27-20. Auburn has not been good for a long time, yet they've still been able to play Georgia competitively in two of their last three matchups. So even though Georgia is a big favorite in this game Auburn might have some confidence that they can play well. The only thing that matters for Georgia is earning another victory, it would be nice though to have a stress free win to sail into the bye week as comfortable as possible. away.headline: Georgia football injury report: Key Georgia defender questionable for Auburn
away.blurb: Per the SEC’s Availability Report, Nate Frazier is expected to be available for Georgia’s game against Auburn on Saturday, but junior safety KJ Bolden is questionable. He’s one of six Bulldogs listed on the report , which was released Wednesday night. Georgia has already ruled out junior wideout Isiah Canion, sophomore wideout Thomas Blackshear, junior running back Chauncey Bowens, junior EDGE Amaris Williams and freshman defensive back Tyriq Green. Junior offensive lineman Marcus Harrison, who has missed the past four games, is considered probable. With Canion out, Blackshear had taken on a bigger role, that was until he suffered a collarbone injury in the Vanderbilt game. The Savannah native caught three passes for 33 yards before leaving the game. Blackshear started his first game in Week 4 vs. Oklahoma. Green should be nearing a return after suffering a high-ankle sprain in Week 2. Green suffered the injury shortly after returning a 93-yard kickoff for a touchdown. He underwent tightrope surgery, but Georgia has no need to rush him back. Green was the Bulldogs’ top kick returner through the first two games. After suffering a torn ACL in spring drills, Williams is likely out for the entire regular season. However, he could return for the postseason. Bowens had Lisfranc surgery and is likely done for the rest of the season. He sustained that injury in Georgia’s win over Vanderbilt in Week 5. Frazier, who hasn’t played since Week 3 against Arkansas, is not listed at all. Bolden is a new addition, but he’s battling a lower-body injury. Canion is in line to miss his fourth straight game with a bone bruise in his knee. He traveled to Arkansas last month as Georgia opened SEC play and got the start. He left that game in the opening series after aggravating the injury. The former Georgia Tech standout hasn’t played since.

away.headline: The Georgia Bulldogs are No. 1 in the AP Poll ahead of the Auburn game
away.blurb: The remaining SEC teams in the AP Poll are Ole Miss (No. 9), Missouri (No. 13), Tennessee (No. 14), and Mississippi State (No. 16). The Florida Gators are out of the polls after losing to South Carolina last Saturday, 38-19. In the latest AP Top 25 , Georgia jumped to the top spot after defeating No. 6 Alabama 20-17. The former No. 1 team, Texas, was defeated by unranked Oklahoma 27-24 on Saturday and dropped six spots to No. 7. The last time Auburn played the No. 1 team in the AP Top 25 was in 2023, when it lost to the Georgia Bulldogs 27-20 in Hugh Freeze's first year as head coach. The last time the Tigers defeated the top-ranked team was in 2017, beating Alabama 26-14. Two weeks before that game, Auburn defeated Georgia, 40-17, when the Bulldogs were ranked No. 1. The AP Poll saw some movement outside of Texas dropping six spots. The LSU Tigers fell the farthest, dropping from No. 10 to No. 22 after their 35-34 overtime loss to unranked Kentucky. However, that win by the Wildcats put them in the rankings at No. 15. Despite losing to Georgia, Alabama stayed at No. 6. away.blurb: Is Chauncey Bowens returning in Week 7? Georgia RB ruled out for Auburn game and beyond Skip to main content About "Georgia running back Chauncey Bowens will miss Saturday’s game against Auburn, and his status moving forward is in doubt, sources tell On3’s Pete Nakos. Bowens suffered a lower-body injury during the Vanderbilt game. A return timetable is unclear at this time," On3's Thomas Goldkamp wrote. Dante Dowdell is out for the season after a freak ATV incident. Nate Frazier has bruised ribs that made him a late scratch against the Crimson Tide. “I feel a little beat up, but through six games I bet everyone is feeling a little bruised up,” Phillips said this week. “I’ll rely on my treatment and feel better. Anything to help my team week in and week out, I’m willing to do.” Omar Mabson II suffered a leg injury against Vanderbilt that didn't keep him out of the Tennessee game. Mabson had a standout performance on Rocky, amassing 62 yards on nine carries. He may be a candidate to have an increased workload. Auburn caught a break ahead of the Deep South's Oldest Rivalry game against Georgia in Week 7. Running back Chauncey Bowens won't be suiting up for the Bulldogs when the two squads collide in Athens. On3's Pete Nakos first reported the news, which spells trouble for Mike Bobo, Kirby Smart, and the rest of UGA's coaching staff beyond this weekend. Bowens missed the Dawgs' 20-17 win over Alabama at Bryant-Denny Stadium this past weekend. He isn't the only Georgia running back who has missed time in 2026. Dwight Phillips Jr. got roughed up against Alabama but plans on playing a large role against the Tigers. Auburn's running back room has had its fair share of injuries as well The Tigers can relate to the Dawgs' injury woes. Jeremiah Cobb is the only healthy running back in the room who's gotten regular reps. USF transfer Nykahi Davenport hasn't seen the field all year. It appears Davenport hasn't earned the reps in practice, since no significant injuries have been reported. Baylor Bryson Washington didn't record any snaps but was on the field against the Volunteers. He had a soft-tissue injury in the offseason. Auburn's running back room has not had a strong performance this season, but the interior offensive line bears some blame. We'll see whose banged-up running back room can give its team the edge this Saturday. Loading recommendations... Please wait while we load personalized content recommendations

home.headline: Kirby Smart says Georgia is 'beat up.' Here's the latest on injuries
home.blurb: “We're a beat up football team right now, guys,” coach Kirby Smart said after the 20-17 win over Alabama. “We've got guys out left and right.” Canion was listed as questionable last week on the SEC Availability Report before being downgraded Friday to out. Blackshear is out with a broken collarbone, according to ABC on Saturday night’s broadcast. The average return to play for contact sports for a broken collarbone is 8 to 12 weeks, according to an Instagram post by Dr. Mike Galbraith, a Texas-based sports medicine physician. Freshman Craig Dandridge played a season-high 55 snaps with Blackshear and Canion out. "We had to go all week kind of not knowing on Isiah," Smart said Monday. "How does it affect you? You talk to Mike (Bobo), you talk to the offensive staff, it's frustrating because you don't really know who's in and who's out. You're trying to make decisions. We thought Nate was going to be able to play. That was a surprise to us. Isiah, we knew it would be close, maybe or maybe not. It just makes it hard because you can't get enough reps for guys." News Sports Entertainment Opinion Real Estate Advertise Obituaries eNewspaper Legals BULLDOGS-EXTRA Kirby Smart says Georgia is 'beat up.' Here's the latest on injuries Marc Weiszer Athens Banner-Herald Updated Oct. 12, 2026, 1:25 p.m. ET Georgia football went on the road and beat Alabama Saturday night with running back Dwight Phillips stepping up in a big way as Nate Frazier was unable to go with injured ribs. The No. 1 Bulldogs are dealing with several notable injuries heading into a week seven game Saturday at home against Auburn. Georgia played its third straight game without Isiah Canion, the transfer wide receiver from Georgia Tech who Smart said Monday is dealing with "a lower extremity injury." The Bulldogs were also without wide receiver Thomas Blackshear, who was injured in the win over Vanderbilt on Oct. 3. Phillips rushed for a career-high 120 yards on 17 carries against Alabama with Frazier and Chauncey Bowens sidelined. Bowens leads the team in rushing touchdowns. He sustained an undisclosed injury against Vanderbilt. Frazier missed the Oklahoma game after being injured at Arkansas and returned to get two second-half carries against Vanderbilt. He was not listed on the availability report all last week, but warmed up and did not play Saturday. ABC’s Holly Rowe said he made a quick cutting move and needed attention from the training staff. Phillips was asked Monday if he had an idea that Frazier wouldn’t be able to go or was surprised. “That’s probably a Kirby Smart question,” he said with a smile.

One of the SEC's best rivalry games returns for the 109th time since 1901, with Alabama and Tennessee playing at Neyland Stadium in Knoxville, Tenn., on Saturday at 3:30 p.m. ET (ABC). A game known as the "Third Saturday in October" for when it's historically been played, the Crimson Tide had been dominating the Alabama vs. Tennessee rivalry during the Nick Saban era, but the programs have split the series over the last four years. Despite the Volunteers catching up to the Crimson Tide in recent seasons, Alabama is a 9.5-point favorite and the popular pick among college football analysts . Alabama vs Tennessee rivalry history: Third Saturday in October 60 (1 win vacated) 40 (1 win vacated) 15 (2007-2021) Longest win streak 7 (1995-2001) Largest margin of victory 992-346-43 (.734) Program record 892-424-55 (.671) Claimed national titles (recognized) Conference championships Heisman winners Consensus All-Americans Weeks in the AP Poll Weeks at No. 1 Bowl games (record) NFL draft picks First-round picks Alabama and Tennessee's rivalry has long been filled with winning streaks, legendary coaches, and cigars. The Crimson Tide and Volunteers played for the first time in 1901, with the programs tying 6-6 in Birmingham, Ala., the home of the rivalry for seven of the first eight meetings. However, the game wasn't initially played on the third Saturday in October (it was played in November), nor every season. For the first 26 years of the rivalry, Alabama and Tennessee played just 11 times, which included the teams not playing at all between 1915 and 1927. Over those first 11 meetings, Alabama went 8-2-1 and didn't allow a Tennessee touchdown from 1903 to 1913. The rivalry returned in full in October 1928, and Alabama and Tennessee have only gone without playing for one season since then, and that was in 1943 due to World War II. The return of the rivalry also coincided with Tennessee becoming a powerhouse under Robert Neyland, who was hired in 1926. That helped Tennessee turn it into a competitive rivalry, with the Volunteers going 20-15-6 from the 1920s through the 1960s. But that's when Alabama changed college football forever after hiring Texas A&M's coach, who had earned his nickname after agreeing to wrestle a bear when he was 13 years old. Paul "Bear" Bryant would beat Tennessee for the first time in 1961 and win on the third Saturday in October 16 times from '61 to '81, taking home six national championships in the process. The rivalry would resume its competitiveness in the 1980s thanks to Johnny Majors, with Tennessee owning Alabama in the 1990s under Phillip Fulmer. But then everything changed when Alabama brought the only college football coach better than Bryant to Tuscaloosa in 2007. Saban went 16-1 against Tennessee. But with Saban gone, the rivalry has been split the last two years under Kalen DeBoer. The first game between Alabama and Tennessee was on Nov. 28, 1901, in Birmingham, Ala. The two programs tied 6-6, the only time both teams scored points in the first 10 meetings. In 1901, Tennessee was held scoreless when Alabama won 24-0, and then the Volunteers shut out the Crimson Tide 5-0 in 1904. From 1905 to 1913, Alabama won seven straight against Tennessee, outscoring the Vols 112-0 (Tennessee would win 17-7 in 1914). After more than a decade-long hiatus, the rivalry returned in 1928 and became one of the top SEC rivalries thanks to Neyland. Why does the winner of Alabama vs. Tennessee smoke victory cigars? One of the most unique aspects of Alabama and Tennessee's rivalry is the victory cigars. The winning team lights up a victory cigar in its locker room following the game, and fans light them up in the stands of the stadium to celebrate a win. The tradition began in the 1950s when Alabama's athletic trainer Jim Goostree began handing out cigars following a win over Tennessee. Both programs continued the tradition, which began as a secret due to NCAA rules around extra benefits for players and use of tobacco products. In 2005, Alabama publicly brought the tradition back to the forefront of the rivalry but had to self-report it as an NCAA violation as a result. However, since 2007, the winner of Alabama vs. Tennessee has knowingly and openly violated the NCAA rule and reported said violation to the NCAA as part of the tradition. Why is it called the Third Saturday in October? This name is pretty self-explanatory, with Alabama vs. Tennessee being played on the third Saturday in October every season. The tradition began when Neyland started consistently scheduling the matchup against the Crimson Tide on the third Saturday in October, with the rivalry officially adopting the name of "Third Saturday in October" in 1939. Though the game hasn't actually always fallen on the third Saturday in October over the decades due to SEC scheduling and conference changes, the rivalry name of the "Third Saturday in October" has remained. Best moments in the Alabama vs Tennessee rivalry The Bear's streak ends (1982) Before Saban, there was Bryant, and the Bear didn't often lose on the third Saturday in October. When he initially took over Alabama in 1958, Bryant got off to a rough start against Tennessee, going 0-2-1. But between 1961 and 1981, Bryant was 16-4-1 against Tennessee, including an 11-game winning streak from 1971 to 1981. In 1982, Tennessee shocked the college football world after ending the streak. The Volunteers' legendary head coach Johnny Majors led his team to a 35-28 upset of No. 2 Alabama. Bryant would return for just one more season in Tuscaloosa, with Majors once again getting the best of the Bear, and Tennessee beating No. 11 Alabama 41-34. The five-overtime game (2003) Tennessee was looking to bounce back from a loss to Alabama in 2002, its first since 1994, in a clash that resulted in the longest game in the history of the rivalry. The No. 22 Volunteers came back from down 20-13 in the fourth quarter when Casey Clausen led a game-tying drive with 30 seconds left to force overtime. Tennessee managed to convert a 4th-and-19 to stay alive during double OT, and in the fifth OT, Clausen scored to pull off a 51-43 win in Tuscaloosa. The game lasted four hours and 53 minutes. The goalposts go for a swim when the drought ends (2022) One of the most improbable wins in the history of the Alabama-Tennessee rivalry came in 2022, when Saban was riding a 15-game winning streak (the longest in the rivalry's history) into Knoxville. Saban had owned the Vols for a decade and a half, recording double-digit wins in 13 of the 15 straight victories and handing Tennessee four of the largest blowout defeats in rivalry history. Landon Kardian Tue, October 13, 2026 at 8:42 PM UTC · 4 min read Advertisement Advertisement About Our Ads College Sports Sports Business Women's Sports College & High School Adventure Sports What & How To Watch Responsible Gaming Share Your Feedback About Our Ads No. 6 Alabama travels to No. 14 Tennessee for a massive SEC rivalry showdown. Can Keelon Russell bounce back and keep the Tide's playoff hopes alive? One of college football's greatest rivalries returns Saturday afternoon as No. 6 Alabama (5-1) travels to Knoxville to face No. 14 Tennessee (5-1) in the Third Saturday in October showdown. Kickoff is scheduled for 3:30 p.m. ET on ABC, and both programs have plenty to prove. Alabama is coming off a heartbreaking 20-17 loss to Georgia, while Tennessee narrowly escaped Arkansas with a 24-17 victory. The Crimson Tide defeated Tennessee 37-20 last season, but the Volunteers have won the last two meetings in Knoxville. With both teams fighting for College Football Playoff positioning, Saturday's matchup could have enormous consequences. Alabama: Can Keelon Russell Bounce Back? Alabama's offense has been one of the nation's most explosive units, averaging 44.2 points per game. Quarterback Keelon Russell has thrown for 1,599 yards, 12 touchdowns, and just two interceptions while adding 225 rushing yards and four scores. However, Georgia exposed some weaknesses in the sophomore quarterback's game. Russell completed just 16 of 30 passes for 185 yards and one touchdown against the Bulldogs, struggling to consistently move the football against an elite defense. Saturday presents another difficult challenge. Tennessee is allowing just 15.5 points per game and has surrendered only three passing touchdowns through six games. Making matters worse, Alabama is expected to be without leading receiver Ryan Coleman-Williams, who has recorded 415 receiving yards and four touchdowns. That means Lotzeir Brooks, who has 389 receiving yards, and Rico Scott will need to step up. The Crimson Tide must also establish their rushing attack to prevent Tennessee from putting all its attention on Russell. Tennessee: The Volunteers Have a MAJOR Problem Tennessee has managed to win five of its first six games, but Josh Heupel's offense has serious questions at quarterback. Freshman Faizon Brandon has battled a shoulder injury, forcing George MacIntyre into his first career start against Arkansas. MacIntyre completed 18 of 29 passes for 247 yards, one touchdown, and two interceptions. And against Alabama's talented secondary, those mistakes could prove extremely costly. The Volunteers rank just 110th nationally in passing offense, averaging 186.5 yards per game. However, Tennessee has been outstanding on the ground. Running back DeSean Bishop has rushed for 678 yards and eight touchdowns, helping Tennessee average 228.3 rushing yards per game. Bishop will be the biggest threat to Alabama's defense, especially considering Georgia rushed for more than 200 yards against the Crimson Tide last weekend. Wide receiver Mike Matthews, who leads Tennessee with 396 receiving yards, could also create problems if Alabama becomes too focused on stopping the run. How Each Team Wins For Alabama, the formula starts with forcing Tennessee to throw the football. If the Crimson Tide can contain Bishop and put the Volunteers into third-and-long situations, their defense should have opportunities to create turnovers. Offensively, Russell must protect the football, utilize his mobility, and attack Tennessee's secondary without forcing unnecessary throws. For Tennessee, everything revolves around establishing the rushing attack and controlling possession. The Volunteers must also generate consistent pressure on Russell and prevent Alabama from creating explosive plays downfield. A loud Neyland Stadium crowd could make things difficult for Alabama, particularly if Tennessee establishes an early lead. I expect a physical, defensive battle between two SEC rivals. Tennessee's rushing attack will create problems early, but I don't trust the Volunteers' quarterback situation against Alabama's defense. Whether it's Brandon or MacIntyre under center, Tennessee simply hasn't demonstrated enough consistency throwing the football. Russell should respond with a much cleaner performance after struggling against Georgia, although I don't expect Alabama's offense to put up its usual explosive numbers. The Crimson Tide will establish a narrow lead before halftime and gradually take control in the second half. I expect Alabama's defense to force multiple turnovers, while Russell makes enough plays to secure a comfortable road victory. Final Score: No. 6 Alabama 24, No. 14 Tennessee 13 Alabama gets back on track, improves to 6-1, and keeps its College Football Playoff hopes alive. Prior to their loss to Georgia, Coleman-Williams had put together a three-game streak of finding the end zone at least once. away.blurb: Alabama football will be without one of its top playmakers for Saturday’s trip to Tennessee . Ryan Coleman-Williams was listed as out for the Third Saturday in October game, when the SEC released its first availability reporter for the matchup on Wednesday. With him out, Alabama will have to get more from some of its other receivers on Saturdays. Rico Scott, Derek Meadows, Noah Rogers and Cederian Morgan could all be in line for more snaps in Coleman-Williams’ absence. Coleman-Williams was one of six Alabama players listed as out. Desmond Umeozulu, Cayden Jones, Nick Sherman, Jeremiah Beaman and Terrance Green are also unavailable. Alabama starting center Racin Delgatty was listed as questionable. Delgatty left the loss to the Bulldogs late with a lower leg injury. Justin Hill appears to be nearing a return as well. The edge was listed as probable on Wednesday’s report. Ahead of the release, UA head coach Kalen DeBoer had foreshadowed Coleman-William’s absence for the game. “Right now we wouldn’t expect him to be with us as far as being on the field,” DeBoer said during his Wednesday radio show. “Going through a few different things, somf from games before, and one from the game on Saturday.” Coleman-Williams was wearing a brace on his right knee for the past two Alabama games. He left the Crimson TIde’s Saturday loss to Georgia looking extremely wobbly after a head-to-head hit that officials did not review for targeting, and DeBoer confirmed after the game the junior wideout had suffered a head injury. Green, a major contributor to the UA defensive line, left the Georgia game with an injury that DeBoer did not specify. DeBoer said he had reaggravated a previous issue. If Delgatty is unable to go, Crimson Tide offensive coordinator Ryan Grubb said that Mal Waldrep will get the nod at center. Alabama head coach Kalen DeBoer spoke with the media on Monday and said that Coleman-Williams was doubtful for this week's game. DeBoer added that the wideout will be considered "week-to-week" after the Tennessee game. Coleman-Williams took a hard hit going up for a reception against the Bulldogs. Can the Tigers pull off another upset, or will the Rebels defend Oxford? Two of the SEC's most intriguing teams are set to collide Saturday afternoon as No. 13 Missouri (5-1) travels to Oxford to face No. 9 Ole Miss (4-1). Both programs are coming off dominant victories. Missouri dismantled Texas A&M 27-6, while Ole Miss embarrassed Vanderbilt 52-17. With both teams sitting at 2-1 in conference play, Saturday's matchup could have major implications for the SEC Championship race and College Football Playoff. Missouri: The Tigers Are Legitimate Contenders Eli Drinkwitz has Missouri playing some outstanding football, particularly on defense. The Tigers are allowing just 17.7 points per game and rank eighth nationally in rushing defense, surrendering approximately 78 yards per contest. Offensively, former Ole Miss quarterback Austin Simmons has thrown for 1,434 yards, 14 touchdowns, and just one interception. Now, he gets an opportunity to prove himself against his former program. But Missouri's biggest weapon has been running back Jamal Roberts. Roberts has rushed for 828 yards and eight touchdowns, including consecutive 200-yard performances. Against an Ole Miss defense allowing 176.4 rushing yards per game, he could be in for another massive afternoon. Former Ole Miss wide receiver Cayden Lee has also been outstanding, recording 42 receptions for 616 yards and five touchdowns. If Missouri establishes its rushing attack early, the Tigers could control this game. Ole Miss: Can Trinidad Chambliss Carry the Rebels? Pete Golding has Ole Miss back in the national conversation following last season's historic playoff run. Quarterback Trinidad Chambliss continues to be one of the most exciting players in college football, throwing for 1,435 yards and 11 touchdowns through five games. Wide receiver Deuce Alexander has emerged as his favorite target, recording 32 receptions for 503 yards and five touchdowns. The Rebels are averaging 38.8 points and nearly 434 yards per game, but their defense remains a major concern. Ole Miss is allowing 28 points per game, including an embarrassing 52-point performance against Florida earlier this season. And facing Missouri's balanced offense certainly won't make things easier. However, the Rebels have been outstanding at home, winning all three of their games in Oxford this season. How Each Team Wins Missouri must establish Roberts early and force Ole Miss into a physical, defensive battle. If the Tigers can dominate time of possession and limit explosive plays from Chambliss, they have an excellent opportunity to leave Oxford with a victory. For Ole Miss, everything starts with its passing attack. Missouri's defense has been elite against the run, meaning Chambliss will likely need to carry the offense. The Rebels must also force Simmons into mistakes and prevent Roberts from consistently reaching the second level. This matchup has all the ingredients for one of the best SEC games of the weekend. Missouri's rushing attack should give the Rebels serious problems, and I expect Roberts to surpass 100 yards once again. However, I trust Chambliss and the Ole Miss offense to deliver when it matters most. The Rebels' explosive passing attack, combined with a sold-out Vaught-Hemingway Stadium, should be enough to overcome Missouri's physicality. Expect a back-and-forth contest that comes down to the final minutes, with Chambliss engineering a late scoring drive to secure the victory. The Rebels enter the game at 4-1 overall and 2-1 in SEC play after dominating Vanderbilt 52-17 last weekend. Missouri arrives in Oxford at 5-1 overall and 2-1 in conference action following an impressive 27-6 victory over Texas A&M. Kickoff is scheduled for 2:30 p.m. CT at Vaught Hemingway Stadium, with the game airing on the SEC Network. With both teams ranked inside the top 15, Saturday’s matchup could be one of the most important games of the weekend. Trinidad Chambliss Leads Ole Miss Ole Miss will once again turn to quarterback Trinidad Chambliss , who has become the key part of the Rebels’ offense. Latest episode SEC Country Podcast New shows Monday & Wednesday Airing It Out with Aaron Murray · Sep 25 The Rebels have shown that they can create explosive plays through the air, and Chambliss has played an important role in keeping the offense productive. Ole Miss will need another efficient performance from its quarterback against a Missouri defense that has been particularly strong against the run. The Tigers are allowing just 78.3 rushing yards per game, making it important for Chambliss to take advantage of opportunities in the passing game. Golding, who took over as Ole Miss head coach, will also want his offense to maintain the physicality and consistency it showed against Vanderbilt. Austin Simmons Returns to Oxford One of the biggest storylines will be Missouri quarterback Austin Simmons returning to face his former team . Simmons previously played for Ole Miss before transferring to Missouri, where he has become the leader of the Tigers’ offense. Through five games, Simmons has thrown for 1,434 yards and 14 touchdowns. He has shown impressive arm talent and the ability to make plays outside the pocket, giving Missouri a quarterback capable of challenging opposing defenses in multiple ways. Simmons completed 14 of 28 passes for 147 yards and a touchdown against Texas A&M, helping Missouri secure a 27-6 victory. Although the passing numbers were not overwhelming, the Tigers controlled the game and delivered one of their strongest defensive performances of the season. Missouri head coach Eli Drinkwitz will look for Simmons to be more efficient against an Ole Miss team that knows his strengths and weaknesses. The familiarity between Simmons and his former teammates adds another layer to an already intriguing matchup. Eli Drinkwitz Has Missouri Rolling Drinkwitz has Missouri positioned for another important season in the SEC. The Tigers have combined a productive offense with a defense that has consistently made life difficult for opponents. Missouri is averaging 35.8 points per game while allowing just 17.7 points per contest. Running back Jamal Rogers has also become a major part of the Tigers’ success, leading the SEC with 828 rushing yards entering the matchup. His ability to control the ground game could be especially important against an Ole Miss defense that has struggled to stop the run at times this season. The Tigers will look to establish Rogers early, allowing Simmons to work from manageable passing situations. A Major SEC Opportunity Ole Miss and Missouri both enter Saturday with plenty to prove. The Rebels want to build on their victory over Vanderbilt and demonstrate that they can compete consistently against ranked SEC opponents. Missouri hopes to continue its strong start and earn another important conference victory on the road. The quarterback matchup between Chambliss and Simmons will be central to the outcome, while the coaching battle between Golding and Drinkwitz adds another compelling storyline. With Missouri’s rushing attack facing an Ole Miss defense that needs to remain disciplined, and the Rebels looking to exploit opportunities through the air, both teams will have important challenges to solve. Saturday’s showdown in Oxford gives Ole Miss a chance to protect its home field, while Missouri arrives looking to prove its 5-1 start is no fluke. The five players who were ruled out are running backs Ahmad Hardy and Malae Fonoti, backup safety JaDon Blair, reserve tight end Gavin Hoffman and right tackle Josh Atkins. The possible designations, from most likely to play to least likely, are as follows: available; probable; questionable/game-time decision; doubtful; out. Texas A&M (3-2, 1-2) listed three players on its final report. Most notably, starting wide receiver Mario Craver is listed as a "game-time decision." Offensive lineman Blake Ivy and wideout Terry Bussey have been ruled out. Drinkwitz just wants them to keep perspective, considering about 20% of FBS players are transfers. "The biggest thing is to not make it bigger than it is," Drinkwitz told reporters Tuesday. "There are great memories from there. I think everybody left there in a positive light on both sides." "We talk about the joy of the journey," Drinkwitz said. "That was a part of their journey that made them who they are right now. I don't think there has to be a whole lot more to it than that." Among the 24 players, eight players start the week on the Wednesday report as “probable,” which means they are more likely to play than not. Eleven players started the week as “questionable,” which is supposed to be close to a 50/50 chance that those players will be able to play. The Tribune is not aware of an update or specific injury for the remainder of the players on the list with questionable or probable designations. Mizzou, as expected, ruled out running backs Ahmad Hardy and Malae Fonoti, right tackle Josh Atkins, reserve safety JaDon Blair and backup tight end Gavin Hoffman for this weekend's game. home.headline: Ex-Rebels lead No. 13 Missouri into Oxford to face No. 9 Ole Miss
home.blurb: Simmons, top receiver Cayden Lee and cornerback Chris Graves Jr. weren't made available to speak Tuesday about transferring from Ole Miss, but it's worth noting that Simmons' Instagram account still has a number of posts from his years in Oxford. "I feel like those guys are definitely going to come out and play with a chip on their shoulder," tailback Jamal Roberts said. "We definitely can let them guys handle that." No. 9 Ole Miss reached the College Football Playoff semifinals a season ago with Trinidad Chambliss at quarterback after Simmons went down early with an injury and lost his starting job. Tigers coach Eli Drinkwitz acknowledged that the game will be a big deal for Simmons, along with two other Mizzou players imported from Ole Miss. Drinkwitz just wants them to keep perspective, considering about 20% of FBS players are transfers. "The biggest thing is to not make it bigger than it is," Drinkwitz told reporters Tuesday. "There are great memories from there. I think everybody left there in a positive light on both sides." "We talk about the joy of the journey," Drinkwitz said. "That was a part of their journey that made them who they are right now. I don't think there has to be a whole lot more to it than that." Mizzou (5-1, 2-1 Southeastern Conference) comes in having won two straight home games against SEC foes, most recently 27-6 over Texas A&M on Saturday. The Tigers' biggest win so far came against Florida, 45-17 on Oct. 3. Simmons has been terrific for the Tigers, ranking 11th in FBS in passing efficiency rating. He's completing 65% of his passes, with 14 touchdowns and one interception in 165 attempts. "He's playing as an experienced quarterback in a really good system," Ole Miss coach Pete Golding said. Lee has scored five touchdowns while leading the Tigers with 42 receptions and 616 yards. He and Simmons may be transfers, but they're already leaders at Mizzou, other players say. Roberts will be another focal point for Ole Miss. After putting together two straight games of 200-plus yards, he ranks first in the SEC and second nationally with 828 rushing yards. Mizzou's top back a season ago, Ahmad Hardy, is recovering from an offseason gunshot wound. Golding said that Ole Miss (4-1, 2-1 SEC) will have its hands full trying to tackle Roberts. "He has the most yards after contact right now, which is something that has been an issue for us on tape," Golding said. With Chambliss continuing to rank as a Heisman Trophy contender and NFL prospect, Ole Miss routed Vanderbilt 52-17 on Saturday. The Rebels also have wins against ranked opponents LSU and Louisville. "They're a total team," Drinkwitz said. "We need to play our best, most complete game to even be in the game." In Mizzou's most recent road game, the Tigers blew a fourth-quarter lead and lost at Mississippi State. Drinkwitz said they had better learn from the experience.
