picks.headline: Oklahoma offense preview: Can Kentucky keep the Sooners struggling
picks.blurb: Oklahoma offense preview: Can Kentucky keep the Sooners struggling - Yahoo Sports Search Query for Search Search Home News Finance Sports More Mail NCAAF College Fantasy Football College Football Playoff Brewers take 3-0 NLCS lead NFL hot seats Champions League results Heisman Watch Story by Wildcats Wire Oklahoma offense preview: Can Kentucky keep the Sooners struggling Braxton Howard, UK Wildcats Wire Wed, October 14, 2026 at 4:11 PM UTC · 3 min read Advertisement Advertisement About Our Ads College Sports Sports Business Women's Sports College & High School Adventure Sports What & How To Watch Responsible Gaming Share Your Feedback About Our Ads Kentucky football travels down to Norman to face the Oklahoma Sooners on Saturday, and both of these teams have plenty of momentum coming into this matchup. Arguably no team in the country has more momentum on their side than the Wildcats right now, coming off back-to-back walk off two-point conversions for the win in overtime. However, Oklahoma came off of their bye week and got a massive win over Texas in the Red River Rivalry game. With that being said, do not let the final score fool you, Oklahoma is still really struggling on offense. Oklahoma's offense will be the worst unit on the field this Saturday, and despite a big 27-24 win over Texas, the issues have not been fixed. The Sooners have scored just six offensive touchdowns since week two. They have only scored over 20 points twice this season, this was week one against UTEP and against Texas where they needed a blocked punt for a touchdown and a pick six to do so. This is a night game in Norman and will present a lot of adversity for Kentucky. The matchup to watch is the Kentucky offense versus the Oklahoma defense, but we will get into that side later. Basically every single offensive metric that you look at to determine offensive success, the Sooners rank bottom five in the SEC. Oklahoma ranks dead last in the conference in all of these statistics: Success rate, Rush SR%, EPA per rush, Explosive play rate and 1D+TD%. They also rank bottom five in the SEC in these statistics: EPA per play, EPA per dropback, Pass SR%, 3rd Down conversion rate, Early Down conversion rate and yards per play. This might be the worst offense Kentucky faces this season unless they can turn things around quickly. Oklahoma ranks first in the SEC in three-and-out rate and negative play percentage. The Sooners have the worst yards per carry average in the FBS. This is a stark contrast because Kentucky's defense ranks top five in the SEC in explosive % allowed and negative % forced. Kentucky's defense has excelled at three things this season: forcing turnovers, forcing negative plays and limiting explosives. This Oklahoma offense has struggled, but they do have some playmakers. The number one guy that should scare you, ironically, is number one Isaiah Sategna. Sategna is a dynamic receiver who is the one guy that can consistently create separation and he is dangerous with the football in his hands. Kentucky has to know where Sategna is on every snap because he is lightning in a bottle when he gets his hands on the football. John Mateer is a reckless but talented quarterback, he made the best throw of his season against Texas to set up the Sooners for the game winning field goal. Mateer threw a perfect back shoulder to Sategna from the far hash. Mateer has arm talent and is a dangerous runner, he immediately looks to run when a pass play breaks down. However, Mateer is extremely turnover prone, even moreso than LSU quarterback Sam Leavitt. Kentucky forced two turnovers on Leavitt, and they need to repeat that on Saturday. They have done a great job of forcing turnovers all season, they did it against Keelon Russell, Marcel Reed, LaNorris Sellers and Leavitt. This defensive line has to get pressure on Mateer to force him to play recklessly. The Wildcats have struggled with scrambling quarterbacks this season, but they were better last week against Leavitt--same thing applies this week with Mateer. Oklahoma as we stated, averages the fewest yards per carry in all of FBS. This is a game where Kentucky should be able to make Oklahoma one dimensional, which is a massive advantage for the Wildcats. The defense has to make Mateer uncomfortable in the pocket and they will have a great chance to win this football game. Kentucky's defense has the opportunity to have their best performance of the season this Saturday. What a wild Saturday it was for the Kentucky Football team. The Wildcats escaped with a 35-34 overtime victory over then-No. 10 LSU Tigers inside Kroger Field while rocking the iconic Power K jerseys. The game featured plenty of twists and turns, including trick plays that resulted in LSU touchdowns, explosive plays from Kentucky’s offense and special teams, turnovers, and, most importantly, missed field goals. Through it all, Kentucky remained competitive. With LSU facing a fourth-down situation late in regulation, the Tigers elected to punt rather than go for it. Kentucky then drove down the field in less than two minutes, setting up kicker Adam Zouagui for a field goal to send the game into overtime after he had missed his previous two attempts. Kentucky won the coin toss and elected to play defense first. LSU quickly drove down the field and scored a touchdown. The Wildcats then got their opportunity, and on third-and-10, quarterback Kenny Minchey connected with Kenny Darby, who nearly took the ball into the end zone but came up a yard short. CJ Baxter immediately punched it in for a touchdown, leaving Kentucky down by one point. Instead of kicking the extra point to force a second overtime, first-year head coach Will Stein decided to go for the two-point conversion to win the game. The decision paid off. Minchey called his own number on a quarterback draw, found plenty of open space, and crossed the goal line untouched to secure the victory. Kentucky defeated LSU 35-34 in overtime, improving to 5-1 overall and 3-1 in SEC play. The Wildcats are now ranked No. 15 in the AP Top 25 poll. Oklahoma Sooners (3-2, 1-1 in SEC) The Oklahoma Sooners have faced increased scrutiny this season after finishing the 2025 campaign with a 10-3 record and earning a spot in the College Football Playoff. However, their season ended with a 34-24 loss to Alabama in the first round, and Oklahoma has struggled to find consistency this year. The potent offense Oklahoma showcased last season has largely been absent throughout the 2026 campaign. The exceptions came in the season opener against UTEP, when the Sooners cruised to a 51-0 victory, and this past weekend, when they defeated then-No. 1 Texas in the Red River Rivalry. However, not all 27 points against Texas came from the offense. Oklahoma scored a touchdown after blocking and recovering a punt in the end zone, while another touchdown came on a pick-six. The Sooners’ other scoring plays included a rushing touchdown and two field goals. Across their other three games, Oklahoma has averaged just 12.3 points per game, which is disappointing for an offense expected to be productive under quarterback John Mateer. Speaking of Mateer, he has completed 90 of 135 pass attempts for a 66.7% completion rate, totaling 1,038 passing yards, eight touchdowns, and four interceptions this season. Mateer is also a running threat, recording 53 carries for 70 rushing yards. Those numbers fall short of his previous two seasons in terms of passing production. In 2025, Mateer threw for 2,885 yards, while he recorded 3,139 passing yards in 2024. His touchdown-to-interception numbers also tell an interesting story. Mateer threw 14 touchdowns and 11 interceptions in 2025, compared with 29 touchdowns and seven interceptions in 2024. For Oklahoma to defeat Kentucky, the Sooners will need Mateer to take another step forward and help their offense become more consistent. For Kentucky to win in Norman, Kenny Minchey and the offense will have to find a way to pierce the Sooners’ stingy defense and avoid game-breaking turnovers that won Oklahoma the game vs. then-No. 1 Texas. As for other notable Oklahoma players, the receiving corps features wide receiver Isaiah Sategna III, Mateer’s primary target, along with tight end Rocky Beers and wide receiver Trell Harris. Kentucky will need to account for all three playmakers while also limiting the Sooners’ running game, which features Lloyd Avant and Jonathan Hatton Jr. Game: Kentucky Football vs. Oklahoma Sooners Location: Oklahoma Memorial Stadium — Norman, Oklahoma Date: Saturday, Oct. 17 Time: 7:30 p.m. ET TV Info: SEC Network will have the TV broadcast Online Streaming: WatchESPN Radio: UK Sports Network Opening Odds: FanDuel lists Kentucky as a 6.5-point underdog . picks.blurb: News Sports Life Business Real Estate Advertise Obituaries eNewspaper Legals SOONERS OU football vs Kentucky TV channel, odds, scouting report for Sooners-Wildcats Colton Sulley The Oklahoman Oct. 11, 2026 Updated Oct. 12, 2026, 2:53 p.m. CT NORMAN — It was thought if Oklahoma could figure out a way to get a win under its belt against Texas that the Sooners could potentially use the victory as fuel to turn around its season. "We needed to get a win for obvious reasons," OU coach Brent Venables said. "I want these guys to experience victory, certainly in this game was incredibly important." Fresh off their emotional Red River Rivalry upset , the Sooners are looking to carry the momentum into Saturday's home game against 5-1 Kentucky . The Wildcats knocked off LSU this past Saturday after converting a two-point try in overtime for the second straight week after UK did the same thing to defeat South Carolina. First-year Kentucky coach Will Stein has been one of the best stories in college football so far this season. OU scored on defense and special teams against the Longhorns and might need to do the same if it wants to win Saturday. The Sooners' offense scored only 13 points, totaling 238 yards but they seemed to find something in the run game with Lloyd Avant, while quarterback John Mateer took care of the football. "We’ve got a really good Kentucky team coming into Norman next Saturday night," Venables said. "Can’t go 8-0 until you go 1-0. Proud of our guys, proud of our coaches for their work, their fight and figuring it out and finding a way to get it done. Enjoy this for a few hours and get back to work. We’ve got a lot of improving. Several guys who didn’t play. They’re really good players. Hopefully we’ll get some guys back here really quick."Here's everything you need to know ahead of Saturday's game: Oklahoma vs Kentucky When: 6:30 p.m. Saturday Where: Gaylord Family — Oklahoma Memorial Stadium, Norman TV channel: SEC Network Line: Sooners by 6.5 Over/under: 43.5 Scouting Kentucky Best player: Quarterback Kenny Minchey might not be the most talented Wildcats player but he's been sensational when it has mattered most. The Notre Dame transfer has completed over 67% of his passes for 1,394 yards, 11 touchdowns and only one interception. He has also been part of both two-point conversions, including his rush up the middle to beat LSU. The case for Kentucky: The Wildcats are no longer just a fun story. Stein has already equaled UK's win total from last season and has his team playing like a legitimate College Football Playoff contender. If Minchey continues to play clean football and Kentucky's defense can force Mateer into mistakes, it could be a long night for the Sooners in Norman. The case for OU: Momentum is a real thing. Maybe the Sooners' rivalry win helps them go on a similar run to that of last year's. Maybe offensive coordinator Ben Arbuckle and Mateer will continue to improve. OU's defense has already proven it's one of the country's elite units and could be a problem for Minchey and the Wildcats. Not to mention the Sooners can create havoc on special teams. home.headline: Michael Fasusi injury update: OU football OL just about ready to return to Sooners
home.blurb: Sooners coach Brent Venables said Tuesday that left tackle Michael Fasusi is "just about ready" to return. Venables added Fasusi has to clear another hurdle or two in the next few days but that he should be ready to be back "soon." Fasusi was initially listed as doubtful to play against Texas last week before being ruled out. The second-year linemen played in 11 games and made 10 starts last season as a true freshman, allowing four sacks on 395 pass-blocking snaps, per Pro Football Focus. "Nobody wishes they're playing more right now than Michael Fasusi," offensive coordinator Ben Arbuckle said. "You should see him at practice. He's always encouraging with great, great energy, great juice. Even whenever we're at a little bit of a low man, he's out there just yelling, 'Thank you, Jesus.' I'm like, OK, I got it. You're right. Thank you, Jesus." "He's great with scheming out things, how they play, how they do what they do," Arbuckle said. "It says a lot about a coach and he does a fantastic job." "I'm excited," Venables said. "Everybody's excited to get another really good player back and he's worked relentlessly. He's in great shape. You saw him in pregame, amped up and ready to go." He appeared to reinjure his shoulder in the Sooners' season-opening win over UTEP after he dealt with an injury during training camp. Getting Fasusi back would do wonders for OU's offense against No. 15 Kentucky at 6:30 p.m. Saturday at Gaylord Family — Oklahoma Memorial Stadium . Venables said he doesn't compare the Sooners' lists with other teams but OU doesn't tackle to the ground in practice and tapers its practices back as the season goes along. picks.blurb: Adam Carriker's Nebraska vs. Oregon Preview and Prediction Skip to main content SI.COM ALL THE GAMES ALUMNI GROUPS FOOTBALL SCHEDULE SI.COM HUSKERS FB BASKETBALL NEWS SI.COM HUSKERS BB Nebraska football is hitting the road for one of its biggest games of the season, and Adam Carriker is breaking it all down on the Carriker Chronicles! Matt Rhule and the Nebraska Cornhuskers are heading to Eugene to face Dan Lanning and the Oregon Ducks in a late-night Big Ten showdown. Both teams are coming off losses, and both have plenty to prove. Can the Huskers bounce back and pull off an upset? Nebraska enters the game at 5-1 after a heartbreaking loss to Curt Cignetti and Indiana. The Huskers showed some good things against the Hoosiers, but once again, they couldn't finish the job. Carriker discusses why Nebraska needs more than another moral victory. At some point, the Huskers have to start winning these big games, especially against talented Big Ten opponents. One of the biggest questions is whether Anthony Colandrea and Nebraska's offense can get things going against Oregon's defense. Colandrea has shown he can make plays, but Carriker believes offensive coordinator Dana Holgorsen needs to put him in good situations, especially on third downs. The Huskers also need production from Jamal Rule and the running back rotation. Can Nebraska establish a running game and keep Oregon's defense guessing? On the other side of the ball, Nebraska's Blackshirts face a major challenge. Oregon has talented receivers who can stretch the field and create explosive plays. Carriker looks at Nebraska's defensive numbers and explains why the Huskers cannot allow Oregon to make big plays over the top. The Blackshirts have been improving, but this will be another serious test of just how far they've come. Carriker also breaks down Oregon's defense, including players like Matayo Uiagalelei and Bear Alexander. The Ducks have plenty of talent, but Oregon has also been unpredictable this season. Nebraska cannot afford to let this become the game where everything suddenly clicks for Oregon. This is also Nebraska's stiffest road test so far this year. Playing in Eugene, in front of a loud Oregon crowd, will test the Huskers' experience and mental toughness. Nebraska has added veteran players who have been through big games before. Now it's time to see whether that experience pays off. Carriker shares his four keys to the game: handle Oregon's crowd, execute in the red zone, prevent big plays and play all four quarters. Nebraska must protect Colandrea, finish drives and avoid the mistakes that have cost the Huskers in close games. Finally, Carriker discusses the point spread and makes his score prediction! He's picking Nebraska to pull off the upset, 24-21! Can Matt Rhule and the Huskers shock Oregon, earn their third Big Ten win and make a statement to the rest of college football? Or will Dan Lanning and the Ducks send Nebraska home with another disappointing loss? Get Adam Carriker's full Nebraska-Oregon preview, breakdown and prediction on the Carriker Chronicles! picks.headline: 'I Will Ride or Die with Anthony Colandrea': Matt Rhule Recaps Nebraska's Loss to Indiana, Previews Oregon
picks.blurb: 'I Will Ride or Die with Anthony Colandrea': Matt Rhule Recaps Nebraska's Loss to Indiana, Previews Oregon Skip to main content SI.COM ALL THE GAMES ALUMNI GROUPS FOOTBALL SCHEDULE SI.COM HUSKERS FB BASKETBALL NEWS SI.COM HUSKERS BB Nebraska head coach Matt Rhule knows 55 minutes of good football isn't enough. It might be against some teams, but not most. As the Huskers look to bounce back from a three-point loss to defending national champion Indiana , Rhule and his staff are making that a point of emphasis for the entire team. At the same time, Rhule is willing to bet on his quarterback to get the job done. Meeting with the media Monday, Rhule reiterated that message and shed light on the Big Red's preparations for its Week 7 road game against the Oregon Ducks. Here's everything he had to say. Anthony Colandrea looks to pass against Indiana. | IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect NU led for much of the game Saturday afternoon, yet the Hoosiers came crawling back. Even when Indiana took the lead late in the fourth quarter, Rhule was still willing to bet on Colandrea to make a play. NU led for much of the game Saturday afternoon, yet the Hoosiers came crawling back. Even when Indiana took the lead late in the fourth quarter, Rhule was still willing to bet on Colandrea to make a play. Asked about going for it on fourth-and-nine, the head coach pointed to what the analytics said: Go for it. It didn't work out this time, but he said he'd do it again. “I just felt like I was going to follow the analytics and put the ball in Anthony’s hands,” Rhule said. “We had holes that we thought were open and felt like, if we wanted to win that game, that ball and that field position, when you needed about 20 yards to kick a field goal, I’m going to put it in Colandrea's hands.” “I don’t always follow the analytics,” he continued. “I felt like our defense would get the stop, but more importantly, I just felt like I needed to put this ball in my guys' hands. I will ride or die with Anthony Colandrea all day, every day.” Indiana head coach Curt Cignetti and FOX Sports' Joel Klatt walk on the sideline during warmups before Saturday's game. | IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect There's no shame in losing to perhaps the best coach in college football in 2026. Still, Nebraska had the Hoosiers on the ropes and failed to put them away. There's no shame in losing to perhaps the best coach in college football in 2026. Still, Nebraska had the Hoosiers on the ropes and failed to put them away. Rhule knows the Huskers need to be better in a few key moments, like that fourth-and-nine, but he doesn't believe the team needs to overhaul much. “When we watched the tape on Sunday, I think you have a team that is angry, who knows they let one get away,” he said. “We’re certainly disappointed, but not discouraged. We also understand that that is what it looks like. You have to not play really well for 55 minutes, you have to play well for 60.” “I think each and every one of us: coaches, staff, players, knows that we have to be one or two plays better,” he continued. “I’ve encouraged the guys to take this time to be one or two plays better, every one of us, so that we can win that game when it comes back in the future.” Kyle Cunanan kicks a PAT last season. | IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect The offense wasn't the only unit that missed an opportunity to make a play. Nebraska's special teams failed to convert a 40-yard field goal late in the first half, a miss that proved costly in the three-point loss. The offense wasn't the only unit that missed an opportunity to make a play. Nebraska's special teams failed to convert a 40-yard field goal late in the first half, a miss that proved costly in the three-point loss. Even so, Rhule still has confidence in his specialists. NU is just 3-for-7 on field-goal attempts in 2026, but the Huskers' head coach said a strong week of practice would influence his decision to trust the kicking game moving forward. “I don’t know if it was perfect, but that’s one we should make,” said Rhule. “I think we’ve had our share of issues so far… We had a missed extra point against Maryland. We had a bad snap against Maryland… I can’t live in a world of confident (or) not confident. I have to err on the side of going for it.” “If we have a great week of practice, then I’ll lean towards that (kicking),” he continued. “But with Anthony, we basically have been like, ‘Hey, we’re going to try to play four downs’. Not because we don’t trust our field goal game, but because we believe in the weapons we have on offense… But yeah, it’s just something we’ve got to get cleaned up this week before we go to Oregon.” Football out west. 🗓️ 10.17.26 ⏰ 10:00 PM CT 🏟️ Autzen Stadium vs Oregon 📺 @CFBONFOX pic.twitter.com/Cy6UNrS913 Nebraska's game at Oregon will feature the latest kickoff time Rhule has ever coached, with the game certain to extend into the early hours of Sunday morning Central time. Fleck had done, I had read some of the things that Charles Huff at Memphis had done, and a lot of it just goes into sleep,” he said. “We’re really asking our guys to go to bed a little bit later each night this week.” “We’re going to finish this game at 2 a.m. our time,” he continued. “Your circadian rhythm starts to shut down, so we’re really just trying, as best as we can, to make 2 a.m. become 12 a.m., make 12 a.m. become 10 p.m. in terms of our bodies this week.” Anthony Colandrea carries the ball against Indiana. | IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect Having a veteran team likely helps, but so does having a quarterback who sets the tone for the entire team. The Nebraska Cornhuskers took the defending champion Indiana Hoosiers to the wire, leading for over three quarters before eventually falling 20-17 to the top five team. But sadly, it wasn't meant to be for Anthony Colandrea (pictured above, pointing to Will Compton en route to a 39-yard touchdown that put the Huskers up 17-6, seemingly icing the game for Big Red) and Company, as Herbert Hoover found Nick Marsh for two fourth-quarter scores, keeping the visitors from Bloomington unbeaten. It was, of course, Nebraska's first loss of the season. This team will go the way of its quarterback. How far can Anthony Colandrea carry the Nebraska Cornhuskers? That depends on if every defense will drop eight into coverage and rush three. Three of those eight in coverage are likely SPIES working for the enemy. Well, spies spying on our beloved quarterback. AC also had a few bad throws, struggling to feed his receivers catchable passes. For the first time this season, Nebraska did not throw a touchdown pass. The running game barely scraped by the century mark. Big plays crushed the defense. But if you looked at this game and don't see progress, you're being willfully ignorant. The Huskers controlled the ball, nearly doubling the time of possession. Nebraska was the more physical team, and the defense shut down two prominent opposing rushers. Now Big Red travels to Eugene to face the Oregon Ducks. Oregon just lost to UCLA, benched Dylan Raiola for a former walk-on, and was bumped from the Top 25. Needless to say, it's been a big week for the Ducks. Let's look at what the experts are saying. Vegas oddsmakers believe that this is a much better Nebraska team than what they predicted in the summer. Before the season, the spread for this game was 21.5 points. Immediately after the Nebraska/Indiana game, the spread was 12.5 points. Then Oregon lost to the Bruins. As of this writing, the FanDuel Sportsbook has the home Ducks as a 7.5-point favorite. The Over/Under is currently set at 52.5 points. Put the coffee on for a long night. Nebraska and Oregon kick off at 10:00pm Central Saturday night.

While it will be a reunion for Oregon football quarterback Dylan Raiola taking on his former school in Nebraska, this college football insider makes a point that it probably won't be him starting on Saturday. According to Justin Hopkins at On3 Sports, the quarterback that "has the leg up" is Brock Thomas, though this is all dependent on whether Dante Moore can come back from a concussion. "Based on what I've heard, Brock Thomas has the leg up," Hopkins wrote. "My bet, today, is that he will be the guy running out with the offense first Saturday night. Watch sports LIVE with fuboTV (free trial) Oregon football's Dylan Raiola was rough in loss to USC As Moore was taken out of the Sept. 26 41-27 win over the USC Trojans with a concussion, Raiola took over and finished off the win, but it was a frustrating effort in the aforementioned loss to UCLA. In that contest, Raiola threw for 43 yards and two picks before being taken out for Thomas, who recorded 156 yards and a touchdown while completing 11 of his 15 pass attempts. While there would be a lot of attention around Raiola starting and playing against his former team in the Cornhuskers, there's a good chance that won't be the reality, especially if Moore came back to play. "This game — of course, it's going to be an emotional game for Dylan, being the place he came from. He's going to do everything he can to make sure our team is in the best situation to have success this week and be prepared. … I know he'll do that because he's a pro," Lanning said Monday, per Pete Nakos. It remains to be seen what the quarterback situation looks like Saturday for the Oregon football program against Nebraska. picks.headline: 4 bold predictions as Oregon football looks to rebound vs. Nebraska
picks.blurb: News Sports Entertainment Life Real Estate Advertise Obituaries eNewspaper Legals FOOTBALL 4 bold predictions as Oregon football looks to rebound vs. Nebraska Alec Dietz Eugene Register-Guard Oct. 14, 2026, 9:01 a.m. PT Oregon football will face Nebraska at home on Saturday, aiming to recover from a recent loss to UCLA. The Ducks are favored, but Nebraska's defense, which ranks in the top 25 nationally, poses a significant challenge. Oregon's quarterback situation is uncertain, with Dante Moore's status unclear due to injury. The Oregon football team , looking to get its season back on track and keep its dwindling College Football Playoff hopes alive following a 17-15 loss to UCLA last weekend , will have just that chance vs. Nebraska Saturday, Oct. 17 at Autzen Stadium. In a rare true night game, the Ducks (3-2, 1-1 Big Ten Conference) will take on a Cornhuskers (5-1, 2-1) squad looking for an upset after coming oh-so-close against Indiana at home last weekend. UO is just more than a touchdown favorite as of Wednesday. "They're playing really, really great on defense," Oregon coach DAn Lanning said. "Very aggressive. They're a good tackling team, they don't give up long runs ... it's a really talented group that we're going to have to play really well for. I know we'll have a great crowd, night game, so that'll be a fun environment for us to be a part of." Oregon vs. Nebraska scouting report Why Oregon has an advantage: Though the Ducks are reeling, especially offensively, Nebraska's offense has been unsteady against better teams, which could play into another tight contest come Saturday. The Cornhuskers are 5-9 since 2023 in Big Ten road games and have been hit or miss against the better teams on their schedule. They took a 10-point second-half lead over Indiana before a late Hoosier comeback. Despite a dismal showing against UCLA, the Ducks still have a top-10 passing offense in the country and take on a somewhat susceptible Cornhusker passing defense. Why Nebraska has an advantage: The Cornhuskers might have lost against the defending champs last week, but proved they could play with the best teams in the country after a 5-0 start to the season. The Ducks, meanwhile, need a big boost of energy after a lethargic showing against UCLA. Nebraska is likely the more confident group and could pounce at the opportunity of attacking a down Oregon team. The Cornhuskers also have one of the best defensive units in the country through six games, ranking in the top 25 in the country in total defense, better than a UCLA group that stymied Oregon last week. Oregon vs. Nebraska injury updates Note: Official availability reports, mandated by the Big Ten, are released every day starting at 5 p.m. Wednesday leading up to kickoff. This story was published before the reports are made public. For Oregon: The good news for Oregon is seemingly, no player suffered a substantial injury in its loss to UCLA last weekend. The bad news is several key contributors were listed as out, including quarterback Dante Moore, with no clear timetable for return. Starting safety Aaron Flowers was also listed as out and Jeremiah McClellan sat with an injury sustained during warmups against Portland State. McClellan is expected to miss much of the season while Moore (concussion) and Flowers' status will be more clear Wednesday. For Nebraska: The Cornhuskers may face the Ducks without one of their best defensive backs in Jamir Conn, who left Nebraska's loss against Indiana with a chest injury and was seen in a sling on the sideline. Key defensive lineman Riley Van Poppel was listed as questionable through the week heading into the game but sat out the loss, as well. It's unclear whether either of those players will be ready to go against the Ducks. Oregon vs. Nebraska: 4 bold predictions If Dante Moore can't play, Dylan Raiola will start against his former team at quarterback Let it be known that Lanning doesn't allow any outsiders at practice. We can only make predictions based on what we've seen in games and what coaches and athletes tell us, so our guess is as good as anyone's who follows along. But if Dante Moore is still recovering from his concussion and is held out against Nebraska this weekend, Dylan Raiola gives Oregon the best chance to win, at least from the onset. Raiola started 22 games for the Cornhuskers before transferring to Oregon and is a former five-star prospect with all the right tools to succeed. He threw for nearly 300 yards and two touchdowns against USC before an absolute stinker against UCLA. Though Brock Thomas gave the Ducks life in the fourth quarter, we think Raiola will get the first nod again, with a much shorter leash if things turn sideways. Oregon's success on first down will determine how its offense performs The Ducks were putrid in almost every aspect through three quarters against UCLA, at least offensively. Worse than maybe everything was how little Oregon managed on first down, leading to third-and-longs it couldn't convert. The Ducks finished 1 for 14 on third- and fourth-down conversions and averaged just 4.4 yards per play. That has to change Saturday, starting with first down players that get the Ducks off to a better start and more manageable later downs. If Oregon can create success on first down and stay on schedule, its offense should see a substantiative boost. Nebraska's Anthony Colandrea will be a much stiffer test than UCLA's QBs With respect to Nico Iamaleava and Ty Dieffenbach, Oregon will be facing a much better quarterback this weekend, at least statistically, in Nebraska's Anthony Colandrea. The senior and UNLV transfer has completed 64% of his throws for 1,406 yards, 13 touchdowns and just three interceptions in six games and rushed for nearly 300 yards and three scores. Colandrea is a true dual-threat playmaker, an QB archetype that Oregon has struggled with this season. Though the Ducks have played good QBs this season like Drew Mestemaker and Jayden Maiava, Colandrea is no slouch and will have success against Oregon's defense Saturday, at points. away.headline: Oregon Ducks make decision on Dante Moore’s status ahead of Week 7 vs. Nebraska
away.blurb: The Oregon Ducks continue to see their College Football Playoff hopes go down the drain as they are sitting unranked heading into Week 7. They are now sitting with a 3-2 (1-1 Big Ten) record thus far after a 17-15 loss last week to the UCLA Bruins. However, they are hoping to get quarterback Dante Moore back on the field after his scary injury the week prior. The program has made a decision on whether Moore will have a chance to play on Saturday against the Nebraska Cornhuskers. Let’s take a deeper dive into what the decision is and what it means going forward for the program and the quarterback. The Oregon Ducks will be without Dante Moore once again in Week 7 The Oregon Ducks have been playing without quarterback Dante Moore due to a concussion he suffered against the USC Trojans. He missed the most recent game, a loss against the UCLA Bruins, but there have been some positive signs regarding his status. However, Oregon would be without the star quarterback for at least another week, per the Big Ten injury report . Moore took to social media recently and shared that he will be back after clearing concussion protocols. “To my team, the community, and to the World, thank you. These past 2 days have been very difficult, but through all of your prayers I have made progress. There’s times I question myself and the Lord and say Why now? but I quickly remember Jeremiah 29:11: “For I know the plans I have for you,” declares the LORD, “plans to prosper you and not to harm you, plans to give you hope and a future”. I can only worry about today, and making sure I give today it’s full attention. I’ll be back soon. Go Ducks!” During the game against UCLA, Dylan Raiola got the start for the Oregon Ducks before being benched and Brock Thomas replaced him with considerably more success. Dan Lanning has not announced who will be starting the upcoming game. Raiola, Thomas, and Akili Smith Jr having all been taking reps throughout practice. It could be getting late early for the Oregon Ducks as they have the No. 25 Northwestern, No. 4 Ohio State, and Michigan all still on their schedule going forward. It will be interesting to see if the program can go on a run and make a push for a second consecutive CFP appearance after being one of the preseason favorites. ・ ‘What About a Third Thing’ – Radio Host Bluntly Floats Possibility of Arch Manning Entering Transfer Portal After 2026 Season ・ “I’m Not Going to Lie” Bulldogs DB Admits He Would Want Pass Interference Called Against Georgia ・ ‘I’ve Got Enough Evidence’ – Colin Cowherd Makes Thoughts Clear on Arch Manning’s Abilities Amid Underwhelming Performances The post Oregon Ducks Make Decision on Dante Moore’s Status Ahead of Week 7 vs. Nebraska appeared first on Gridiron Heroics .
